content:
**Hydration guard shipped — the #820 race is a skip, not a duplicate (#820)**

**What**: `importMemory` now holds a machine-scoped, non-blocking guard (lib/hydration-guard.mjs, mkdir-atomic under os.tmpdir()) across its read-to-write window; a second importer returns deferred+contended and warns on stderr (i18n memory.import.contended). Stale guards (dead pid or >10 min) are reclaimed. Header comment at the import site names the twin hazard and states this is mitigation; the fix is #863's idempotent hydration.

**Why**: Memory 2.0 Wave 0 (#864 task 0.1). The import TOCTOU fired three times on 2026-09-01.

**Where**: brain/scripts/memory/lib/hydration-guard.mjs (+test, 8), brain/scripts/memory/backends/engram.mjs importMemory (+4 tests incl. the #820 shape), i18n en/es, openspec/changes/issue-820-import-hydration-guard.

**Learned**: (1) Keep the critical section synchronous end to end so no await can interleave a second importer — and so the race is expressible with sync seams. (2) Tests that fake the backend must fake the guard (`_guard: noGuard`); otherwise the suite takes the real machine lock and can make a real session:start report contended. (3) Reproduced live: two concurrent `cli.mjs import` → one completes, one SKIPPED, lock released, store unchanged. (4) The lock is NOT under .memory/ (per-worktree, guards nothing) nor under the backend's dir (#863's no-artifact rule).
